events.text:
The next part is a tracker optimisation task:

- you are allowed to change the radii of the barrel layers and the z-positions of the disks, but not the envelopes
- use Fatras + truth tracking + residuals as shown above 
- module types stay unchanged, stave general structures as well, but the number of staves could be changed if needed
- hit coverage should be kept as high (or increased)
- exceptionally for the pixel endcaps the introduction of a new disk is allowed (which for simplicity for the moment will have a homogenous material disk behind similar than the other pixel disks in order to avoid material mapping for this step)



The task is the following:

- optimise the d0 and z0 resolution (mostly dominated by innermost layers)
- keep (or improve) the momentum resolution
- try to keep a >= 10 hit coverage throughout the detector acceptance

I’ll use the validated 3 T Fatras truth-tracking chain as the reference, check the layout and envelope constraints, and define candidate changes for comparison. I’ll track hit coverage alongside d₀, z₀, and momentum resolution so the tradeoffs stay visible.

For the optimisation, should the primary performance comparison use geometric digitization with the frozen cluster-size error table, or the Gaussian-smearing chain? I recommend geometric digitization, with Gaussian smearing as a cross-check. I’ll otherwise keep constant 3 T, muons at pT 1/10/100 GeV, and |η| ≤ 4 from PR #101.
- Geometric primary; Gaussian cross-check
- Gaussian primary; geometric confirmation

PR #101 is merged, and I’ve started a separate optimisation branch from it. I’m using the repository’s coordination and validation workflow to check geometry constraints, native execution, and performance measures in parallel.

The material treatment needs care: moving a layer also moves its material. I’ll check how to transport the existing material profiles consistently, including the allowed homogeneous material behind any new pixel disk. The Spack setup still reports changed fingerprints, so I’ll verify the existing runtime before using it.

The baseline’s main coverage gap is forward: only about 51–52% of tracks at \(3<|\eta|<3.5\) produce ten measurements. An extra pixel disk alone cannot close that gap, so I’m screening disk positions as well as the inner barrel radii. The beam pipe and stave supports also limit how far the first pixel layer can move inward.

I’ll use geometric digitisation with the frozen PR #101 error table for the primary comparison. Material profiles will move with their corresponding layers, with every transfer audited.

Two useful trials are emerging: a modest inward move of the first pixel barrel plus a disk at \(|z|=900\) mm, and a rearranged pixel disk schedule aimed at forward coverage. The latter may sacrifice measurements near the barrel/endcap transition, so both coverage and resolution need checking.

Confirmed: geometric digitisation will be primary, with Gaussian smearing as the crosscheck.

I’m also checking whether fewer staves could allow the outer pixel barrel layers to move inward while retaining their local construction. That could recover transition-region hits lost by a forward disk schedule; candidates with stave or support collisions will be rejected.

The first compact barrel trial failed a support check: adjacent staves cleared, but annular supports intersected the next layer near the barrel ends. I’ve retained it as a rejected trial and am checking slightly larger radii. The comparison code is ready to retain failed fits, low-hit events and momentum tails in the results.

The native control smoke test passed: 100 generated muons produced 100 fitted tracks with no invalid covariances. The new study driver also reproduced the baseline compact, material map and calibration semantically.

The compact barrel proposal has hit another constraint: its shifted cable bands intersect outer layers. I’m keeping that rejection and testing a less aggressive inward layout alongside the disk trials.

The finite-patch screen found a promising disk schedule, with roughly 99% ten-hit coverage in its reference subset. That is only a search result: it uses straight rays and omits material and curvature. It now gives us a focused candidate to test with Fatras at all three momenta.

For the added disk, I’m using disk 2 as the material template. Disk 1’s mapped profile includes much more barrel-transition material, which would overstate the material of a standalone disk.

The selected coverage candidate passed native construction and a 100-event smoke test, including the extra disk pair and its downstream homogeneous material. It retains the outer pixel radius at 182 mm and uses 32/57/85 mm for the first three barrel layers.

The exploratory campaign is now running: five layouts, each with 2,000 muons at 1, 10 and 100 GeV. It compares the inner barrel changes, the added disk alone and the rearranged disk schedule.

The exploratory fits are completing. A fuller geometry audit caught an omitted attachment: disk collectors still sit at their original z positions after the disks move. I’m correcting those placements before confirmation. The exploratory Fatras results use the sensitive surfaces and effective material profiles, so I’ll retain them with that limitation and rerun the final comparison from the corrected geometry.

The first Fatras comparison shows a tradeoff: the coverage-focused layout reaches about 99% ten-hit coverage, but worsens forward d0 and momentum resolution. It does not meet the combined objective.

I’m testing a balanced layout that keeps the first disk and the farthest disk at their baseline positions. That preserves the forward lever arm and avoids moving the heavy barrel-transition material profile into the first forward measurement.

The corrected coverage layout now passes the full native overlap check with zero overlaps. The balanced trial also looks more promising: about 98.4–98.9% ten-hit coverage, with improved d0 and z0 widths in many regions. Momentum still needs confirmation.

The layouts are now frozen for independent-seed runs with 10,000 muons per case, using geometric digitisation and the requested Gaussian crosscheck.

The study is now in draft [PR #104](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/104). It includes the code, configurations, exploratory results and rejected geometry trials.

Both corrected candidate compacts pass the full overlap check. I’m also testing a late-disk control to see whether adding the measurement after most of the momentum lever arm reduces the low-momentum cost. It has a separate validation seed reserved, so it won’t be selected using the running confirmation results.

The main geometric comparison is complete. The smaller pixel change improves the impact-parameter resolutions and raises ten-hit coverage substantially; the more aggressive layout shows a low-momentum regression. I’m finishing the Gaussian cross-checks and the separately seeded late-disk study before settling the recommendation.

All 300,000 confirmation events have now finished, and the candidate compacts pass the full native overlap check. The ten-hit target still has gaps: the mild layout reaches about 97% overall, but falls short in parts of the forward acceptance. I’ll make those gaps explicit alongside the resolution gains.

The Gaussian cross-check adds a qualification: the mild layout’s 1 GeV momentum width is about 4% worse, although its impact-parameter widths improve overall. The late-disk alternative also has forward regressions. The study therefore identifies useful tradeoffs, but no tested layout meets every objective. I’m retaining the full distributions and adverse results in the PR.

The independent scientific check has reproduced the native counts, residuals, pull histograms, material transfers and calibration audits. The report now separates core-width gains from the long momentum tails, and records the remaining forward coverage deficit. I’m finishing the physical assessment, accounting records and hosted checks.

The physical assessment is complete: both reviewed candidates reproduce the audited geometry byte for byte, with fixed envelopes and unchanged local module structures. All 20 controls pass in the native environment. Service routing and capacity remain unqualified, and the material treatment remains an approximation; both limits are explicit in the report.

The report and full residual/pull distributions are retained, and PR #104 now describes the confirmed results and limitations. I’m synchronizing the final specialist assessments and exact usage records. The coordinator turn is still active, so its token count remains excluded.

pull_request.title: Tracker: optimise impact-parameter resolution and hit coverage within fixed envelopes
pull_request.head: codex/tracker-resolution-optimization
pull_request.body:
Explore tracker placements within fixed envelopes using constant-3T Fatras truth tracking, geometric primary digitisation and a frozen-error Gaussian cross-check. The isolated study completes 48,000 exploratory and 300,000 confirmation events. DES-040 remains DRAFT/PROTOTYPE; production geometry is unchanged.

The mild candidate moves the first pixel barrel from 34 to 32 mm and adds one mirrored donor2 pixel disk at |z|=900 mm, with homogeneous material behind its sensitive faces. It improves global geometric d0 core widths by 2.4–5.1% and z0 by 3.7–6.5%, and raises ten-hit coverage from about 88% to 96.5–96.8%. Balanced and late-disk alternatives are retained as tradeoffs.

**No tested layout meets every objective.** Mild has a Gaussian 1 GeV momentum-width regression of 4.0%, forward ten-hit holes remain, and high-pT nonlinear residual tails prevent full-distribution momentum-preservation claims. Balanced has a resolved primary 1 GeV momentum regression. Full tails, wrong charge, fit/selection failures, all-generated coverage, all-eta pulls, regional intervals and rejected trials are retained.

The tools regenerate native Gen3 portal/calibration identities by physical roles, audit effective material inventories and preserve local module/stave structures. Disk-owned collectors and rail slots follow their stations. Full native ROOT overlap/extrusion checks find zero intersections at 1e-5 mm for the corrected candidates. Material relocation, frozen response and service connectivity/capacity remain qualified approximations; no engineering sign-off or integration is implied.

- Governing design: [DES-040](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/tracker-resolution-optimization/docs/design/DES-040-tracker-resolution-optimization.md), issue #103.
- [Results, figures, exact source/data identities and limitations](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/tracker-resolution-optimization/docs/validation/tracker-resolution-optimization/README.md).
- [Complete confirmation tables and regional exceptions](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/tracker-resolution-optimization/docs/validation/tracker-resolution-optimization/confirmation-tables.md).
- [Reproduction](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/tracker-resolution-optimization/software/analysis/tracker_optimization/README.md).
- Validation: 20/20 native controls; portable controls with the expected native-helper skip; all 30 confirmation source/native/output audits pass. CI replays retained evidence without native dependencies. Separate SysArch and PhysVal assessments are recorded in the task journal.
- Curated interactions and observed completed-turn accounting are synchronized; the active coordinator turn remains excluded until finalized.

Refs #103.
